name: WI-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Scott Fitzgerald with $1.3M war chest vs. $3K for Democrat Andrew Beck
Polymarket prices Fitzgerald at 96% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Fitzgerald: an R+11 district, incumbency, and a roughly 400-to-1 cash advantage over Beck, with prediction markets pricing his win odds near 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of about R+15.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Beck within single digits, or a major outside-spending intervention, would be the first sign the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Fitzgerald, the incumbent Republican, seeks reelection in a Wisconsin district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.3 million on hand after raising $1.4 million, while Democratic challenger Andrew Beck has raised about $15,000 and holds just over $3,000. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Fitzgerald about a 96 percent chance of winning. The expected margin sits near fifteen points in Fitzgerald's favor, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling. Beck would need an unusual shift in the district or substantial outside investment to make this competitive, and neither appears on the horizon.
